answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared contract before bidding. The stake cannot back another identity while locked, and a proven failure to deliver forfeits it to the buyer. A relic seller on a trading ledge therefore gains no free haven by spawning accounts: each account ties up fresh capital, and each provable fraud risks losing its stake. Honest pseudonyms remain possible, but mass impersonation becomes expensive.
